description: SovereignGuard GenAI Payment Fraud Attack Knowledge Base. Each entry describes a fraud pattern the Red Team can synthesise, the payment surfaces it targets, the behavioural changes it induces in the event stream, and the signals a defender would hope to see. Everything here is a simulation specification — no entry contains operational guidance for committing fraud.

difficulty_levels.EASY: Blatant execution. Attacker makes no attempt to blend in: unfamiliar device, unfamiliar geography, amount far outside the victim's range, immediate escalation.
difficulty_levels.MEDIUM: Partial evasion. Attacker controls one or two obvious signals but still trips others.
difficulty_levels.HARD: Deliberate mimicry of legitimate behaviour. Familiar device or geography, amounts inside the victim's plausible range, patient pacing across hours or days.
difficulty_levels.ADVERSARIAL: Generated by the adaptive feedback engine against a specific measured weakness of the deployed detector. Parameters are chosen because the detector has already been observed to miss them.

genai_amplification_note: Generative AI does not invent new payment rails; it collapses the cost of personalisation, translation, voice cloning and iteration. The practical consequence for a defender is a shift from a few high-volume templates to very many low-volume variants. That is why this taxonomy is parameterised rather than enumerated: the Red Team samples the parameter space instead of replaying fixed scripts.

attacks.target: Customer account and its outbound payment capability
attacks.genai_role: Credential-stuffing lists triaged by a model; session-aware phishing pages generated per-victim; voice clones used to defeat call-centre reset controls.
required_conditions: Victim account has outbound transfer capability
Attacker controls a session or credential set
behavioural_changes: Login from a device with no history on the account
Credential or profile mutation shortly before value movement
Beneficiary added minutes before first use
Small probe transaction preceding escalation
Monotonically escalating amounts within one session or day
attacks.hard_variant_note: The dangerous version reuses a device already on the account (session hijack rather than new-device login), keeps every amount inside the victim's own historical range, and spreads the drain across days so no 24-hour velocity window looks abnormal.
mitigations: Cooling-off window between payee creation and first high-value use
Step-up authentication bound to credential-change recency rather than amount alone
Behavioural-biometric continuity check inside the session
Cumulative-drain limits measured over 7 days, not 24 hours

attacks.target: The fraud engine's own thresholds and velocity windows
attacks.genai_role: Automated probing of a defence's decision boundary: the attacker submits variations, observes which are approved, and lets a model infer the accepted region.
required_conditions: Attacker already has payment capability on the account
behavioural_changes: Amounts parked just beneath round-number review limits
Value split across many transactions instead of one
Deliberate inter-transaction delays to defeat fixed velocity windows
Rotation across merchants, methods and channels to fragment the trail
attacks.hard_variant_note: Each individual transaction is unremarkable by construction. Only the aggregate over a longer window, or the unusual regularity of the spacing, distinguishes it from ordinary spending.
mitigations: Aggregate value features over multiple horizons (1h / 24h / 7d / 30d)
Detect regularity itself — human spending is bursty, scripts are periodic
Avoid publishing or leaking decline reasons that reveal the boundary

attacks.genai_role: Fabricated but internally consistent identity packages — coherent name/address/employment sets, generated document images, and generated selfie or liveness media for KYC.
required_conditions: Onboarding accepts document evidence without authoritative-source verification
Identity has no contradicting bureau record
behavioural_changes: Very short digital footprint relative to claimed age
Low document-verification confidence with no adverse record
Poor contactability across channels
A deliberate 'good behaviour' cultivation period before bust-out
Terminal bust-out consuming most of the available limit
attacks.hard_variant_note: A patient synthetic identity behaves better than a real customer for months. Detection has to come from origination-time evidence and footprint sparsity, because the transaction stream looks exemplary right up to the bust-out.
mitigations: Verify against authoritative sources rather than document appearance
Score footprint consistency: age claimed vs. age evidenced
Treat unusually clean early behaviour on a thin file as its own signal
Velocity limits on limit growth for thin-file accounts

attacks.target: The acquiring side: merchant onboarding and settlement
attacks.genai_role: Complete storefronts, product catalogues, review corpora, invoice templates and support personas generated in minutes, making a fraudulent merchant indistinguishable from a new legitimate one on surface features.
required_conditions: Self-serve or aggregator onboarding with light verification
behavioural_changes: Newly registered merchant taking immediate volume
Almost every payer is a first-time customer
Ticket sizes inconsistent with the declared category
Card-not-present share near total
Volume ramp then disappearance before chargebacks land
attacks.hard_variant_note: The evasive version ages the merchant record first and mixes in genuine-looking low-value traffic, so merchant age and chargeback rate look acceptable when the ramp begins.
mitigations: Hold settlement on thin-file merchants until chargeback maturity
Monitor first-time-payer concentration per merchant
Cross-check ticket distribution against declared category
Beneficial-ownership verification at onboarding

attacks.attack_name: AI-Generated Phishing and Malicious Payment Links
attacks.target: The customer's intent — the payment itself is genuinely authorised
attacks.genai_role: Per-victim message generation in the victim's language and register, cloned brand pages, and rapid rotation of infrastructure so no single template accumulates a reputation.
required_conditions: Customer can be reached on a messaging channel
Payment can be initiated from an inbound link or collect request
behavioural_changes: Payment initiated from an inbound link rather than customer navigation
Beneficiary or merchant never seen before on the account
Compressed session — little browsing, immediate payment
Amount often just under a psychologically checkable figure
Frequently outside the customer's habitual hours
attacks.hard_variant_note: Because the customer authorises willingly, every authentication control passes. The only available evidence is contextual: how the payment was initiated, and how unlike the customer's habits the counterparty is.
mitigations: Treat link-referred initiation as a distinct risk context
In-flow warnings naming the actual payee for first-time counterparties
Payee-name / account-name confirmation before submission
Reputation on the initiating link infrastructure, not just the payee

attacks.attack_name: AI Social Engineering and Voice-Clone Impersonation
attacks.target: The customer's decision-making under manufactured urgency
attacks.genai_role: Real-time voice cloning of a family member, bank official or executive; a conversational agent that sustains a long call, adapts to objections, and coaches the victim through the bank's own warnings.
required_conditions: Live channel to the victim (call, video or chat)
behavioural_changes: Payment authorised while an inbound call is in progress
Victim's own device, own location, own credentials — nothing is compromised
Beneficiary created during the call
Amount far above the victim's norm, often the account's practical maximum
Sometimes a sequence of transfers as the story escalates
Elevated behavioural-biometric deviation from stress and dictation
attacks.hard_variant_note: The hardest version keeps the amount inside the victim's plausible range and uses an existing beneficiary, removing the two strongest signals and leaving only the call-in-progress context and biometric stress.
mitigations: Call-in-progress detection wired into the payment flow
Mandatory delay on first payment to a newly created payee
Named-scenario warnings rather than generic caution messages
Out-of-band confirmation on high-value first-time transfers

attacks.target: The seams between controls that each only see one stage
attacks.genai_role: Orchestration. A planning model sequences steps across channels and time so that no single control sees enough of the pattern to act, and adapts the plan when a step is challenged.
required_conditions: Controls evaluate events in isolation rather than as a campaign
Attacker can operate patiently across days
behavioural_changes: Each stage individually defensible; only the ordering is incriminating
Reconnaissance and mule preparation precede any value movement
Value fans out to multiple beneficiaries that converge downstream
Long deliberate pauses between stages
Cross-surface hops so no single channel holds the full trail
attacks.hard_variant_note: This is the pattern that most clearly defeats per-transaction scoring. Detection requires either sequence modelling on the account timeline or graph features across beneficiaries — a single-row classifier is structurally unable to see it.
mitigations: Score the account timeline, not only the transaction
Beneficiary in-degree and mule-convergence graph features
Persist a per-account risk state that decays slowly across days
Correlate events across channels into one campaign view

cross_cutting_patterns.name: ADAPTIVE_FRAUD
cross_cutting_patterns.description: Not a separate attack type but a property an attacker can apply to any of the above: observe which variants are approved and shift the distribution toward the accepted region. This is what the adaptive feedback engine simulates, and the reason a static benchmark overstates a detector's real-world durability.
cross_cutting_patterns.implication: A detector must be re-evaluated against attacks generated after it was trained, not only against the distribution it was trained on.

cross_cutting_patterns.name: DEEPFAKE_MEDIA
cross_cutting_patterns.description: Voice and video synthesis used as the delivery mechanism for SOCIAL_ENGINEERING and SYNTHETIC_IDENTITY. This platform models its downstream effect on the payment event stream rather than the media itself, since the payment system only ever observes the resulting transaction.
cross_cutting_patterns.implication: Media-authenticity controls sit upstream; the payment layer must still be able to catch what gets through.
